description: Turn PowerPoint slides into a Markdown outline: slide titles, bullet points and speaker notes, ready to paste into an AI chat. Free, nothing uploaded.
heading: PowerPoint to Markdown
subtitle: Turn a slide deck into a Markdown outline with titles, bullets and notes; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Convert a PowerPoint deck to Markdown when you want to paste its words into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini to summarise, rewrite or check them. Open a .pptx, .ppsx, .potx or .pptm file and it becomes an outline: the deck's name as # heading, each slide as ## Slide N with its title, the slide's text as bullet points, and the speaker notes as a quote under the slide. The outline appears in a text box with its token count. The file is read by your browser and never uploaded, and nothing is sent to any AI service.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert PowerPoint to Markdown

steps.title: Open your deck
steps.text: Choose or drop a .pptx, .ppsx, .potx or .pptm file, or try a sample.

steps.title: Read the outline
steps.text: Each slide appears as a ## heading with its text and notes, with the token count shown.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.text: Click Copy to paste the outline into an AI chat or a document, or download the .md file.

handles: Structure: # for the deck's name, ## Slide N: title for each slide.
Slide text: the words in text boxes and placeholders, as bullet points.
Speaker notes: written as a > quote under their slide.
Arabic and other right-to-left text, kept in its reading order.
limits: Pictures, charts, SmartArt and the slide layout are left out; only the words are kept.
Old .ppt files are not read; save them as .pptx in PowerPoint first (checked 24 November 2026).
Text inside pictures can't be read, because it is part of the picture, and the labels and numbers of charts are not read.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your deck is read and converted by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. Nothing is sent to any AI service either: you choose where to paste the outline.

faq.question: What does the outline look like?
faq.answer: The deck's name as a # heading, then ## Slide 1: and the slide's title, the slide's text as - bullet points, and the speaker notes as a > quote. The same pattern repeats for every slide.

faq.question: Are speaker notes included?
faq.answer: Yes. They are often where the real explanation is, so they come out as a quote under their slide.

faq.question: Why are charts and pictures missing?
faq.answer: The outline carries only the words on the slides and in the notes. A chart's labels and numbers are kept in the file apart from the slide text and are not read, and the text inside a picture is part of the picture, so it can't be taken out.

faq.question: Can I see the slides themselves?
faq.answer: Yes. The PowerPoint viewer shows every slide as it was designed, in your browser.

faq.question: Should I check the slides for personal details first?
faq.answer: If the slides hold customer names, emails or phone numbers, check them first. Mask data hides names, emails, phone numbers and IDs in CSV, Excel, JSON and text files.

faq.question: How do I get the text out of a PowerPoint file?
faq.answer: Copy the text from each slide by hand, or turn the whole deck into an outline at once with a PowerPoint to Markdown converter. OpenAnyDoc does it in your browser, with slide titles, bullet points and speaker notes, ready to copy or download as .md, and nothing is uploaded.
